effectIntent: A fantasy knight deploys a massive protective barrier between caster and target. Its surface normal follows the caster-to-target direction, so the shield faces the enemy instead of the sky and reads as a physical interception plane from a strict top-down action-RPG camera.

silhouette.primaryMass: foreshortened convex mantlet or curved barrier with a clearly visible caster-facing root, target-facing leading edge, and readable thickness
silhouette.asymmetry: the leading edge, compression, and side shoulders establish one enemy direction without splitting the barrier into mirrored lobes
connections: four large ornaments or braces must grow from the barrier shoulders and rim instead of floating around it
the structural root visibly anchors the barrier on the caster side
all energy gaps terminate inside a continuous load-bearing frame
motifs: one broad knight-mantlet mass with a directional leading ridge
four integrated protective shoulders with stronger weight toward the target

depthLayers.role: narrow grounding and caster-side seating cue, never a radial magic circle
dominant curved enemy-facing protective surface with readable opacity and thickness
continuous gold root, shoulders, leading rim, and four connected braces
restrained leading-edge highlight that reinforces the target direction

materialZones.finish: deep translucent emerald with broad dual-scale internal noise, slow directional flow, and nonuniform opacity

materialZones.role: root, shoulders, braces, and leading rim
materialZones.finish: warm solid metal response with narrow emissive seams and controlled moving highlights
thin Fresnel-like response plus a directional dissolve band, never uniform emission across the body
soft dark-green occlusion and a short contact wedge without circles or glyphs

forbiddenTraits: shield face aimed upward at the sky
complete heraldic disc presented to the top-down camera
ground sigil or radial UI medallion silhouette
small repeated runes, glyphs, or filigree
particles used to hide weak geometry
literal copying of GNF_ or third-party VFX assets
acceptanceQuestions: Without an arrow label, can a reviewer identify the caster side, target side, and shield normal?
Does the shield intercept the line between caster and target instead of lying on the ground or facing the sky?
At gameplay scale, does one dominant barrier mass read before the braces and highlight layers?
Are all four braces visibly load-bearing parts of the frame rather than detached glyphs?
Does the silhouette remain attractive and directional with all Shader color removed?
Do the proposed material zones separate body, edge, metal, and contact instead of using one flat glow?
Can the caster and target remain readable around or through the barrier?
